grade.first_issue: The proof merely asserts that the proposed radius makes the tangency quadratic vanish; the single trigonometric identity and equilateral example do not supply the required general calculation.
grade.summary: The reduction of the rhombus condition to a target radius is useful, but the central tangency verification is omitted. Moreover, positivity of both roots does not prove that the proposed radius is the smaller root selected by the proximity condition.
strengths: Correctly reduces the desired rhombus condition to \(AX=r\cot A\) in the relevant acute-\(A\) case.
Sets up a plausible coordinate quadratic encoding external tangency.

errors.description: The load-bearing substitution showing that \(\rho=\frac{r\cos A}{2\cos^2(A/2)}\) satisfies the tangency equation is asserted without the substantial algebra needed to verify it.
After establishing only that both roots are positive, the solution gives no comparison proving that the proposed root is the smaller one or that the stated proximity condition selects it.
The formulas for the Euler-circle center’s projection and distance are introduced without derivation, although they are essential to the quadratic argument.
